skill.description: Guide for using PySAM to read, write, and analyze genomic SAM, BAM, CRAM, VCF, BCF, FASTA, and FASTQ files.
skill.summary: Use PySAM for genomic file access, sequence extraction, variant processing, coverage analysis, and indexing workflows.

content.value_statement: Genomic data workflows need reliable handling of BAM, VCF, FASTA, and FASTQ files. This skill guides PySAM usage for reads, variants, sequences, coverage, and indexing.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to open and query SAM, BAM, and CRAM alignment files.
Shows how to read, filter, and write VCF and BCF variant records.
Guides FASTA sequence extraction and FASTQ read processing with PySAM.
Documents coverage, pileup, and read-depth workflows for genomic regions.
Covers tabix, BAM, FASTA, and VCF indexing requirements.
Provides integrated examples that combine reads, variants, and reference sequences.
limitations: It is documentation and examples, not a full variant caller or aligner.
Large genomic files still require local storage, indexes, and adequate memory.
Coordinate systems differ across PySAM calls, VCF records, and region strings.
Examples must be adapted to each laboratory file layout and reference genome.

use_cases.title: Review Alignment Quality
use_cases.description: Calculate read counts, mapping rates, duplicate rates, and coverage summaries from BAM or CRAM files.

use_cases.title: Inspect Variant Evidence
use_cases.description: Combine VCF records with BAM read support and reference context for targeted variant review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sequence Extracts
use_cases.description: Extract reference intervals, gene sequences, or filtered reads for downstream analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Open an Alignment File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PySAM to open a BAM file and list reads overlapping chr1 from 1000 to 2000.

prompt_templates.title: Filter Variant Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to read a VCF file and keep variants with quality at least 30 and depth at least 20.

prompt_templates.title: Measure Regional Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PySAM workflow that reports per-base coverage and low-coverage intervals for a target region.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate BAM, VCF, and FASTA
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PySAM workflow that validates variants with aligned reads and extracts reference sequence context.

output_examples.input: Summarize coverage for chr7 from a BAM file.
output: Coverage summary for chr7 target interval.
Mean depth is reported with minimum and maximum depth.
Low-coverage intervals are listed for follow-up review.

output_examples.input: Explain how to extract variants in genes from a VCF and BED file.
output: Open the VCF with PySAM VariantFile and the BED file with TabixFile.
Fetch variants for each gene interval using matching contig, start, and end coordinates.
Return gene names, variant positions, alleles, and quality fields.

output_examples.input: Help avoid coordinate mistakes when using PySAM.
output: Use zero-based, half-open coordinates for numeric PySAM calls.
Use one-based coordinates for region strings and VCF positions.
Document every conversion near the query that uses it.

best_practices: Create and verify indexes before using random access queries.
Keep coordinate conversions explicit when moving between BAM, VCF, and region strings.
Stream large files with iterators and close file handles after processing.
anti_patterns: Loading entire BAM, FASTQ, or VCF files into memory for simple filters.
Mixing zero-based and one-based coordinates without comments or tests.
Writing output files before validating headers, contigs, and sample names.

faq.question: What genomic files does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers SAM, BAM, CRAM, VCF, BCF, FASTA, FASTQ, BED, GTF, and tabix-indexed files.

faq.question: Does this skill download data from the internet?
faq.answer: No. The documented fetch methods read local indexed genomic files by genomic region.

faq.question: Why are index files important?
faq.answer: Indexes allow fast random access to large BAM, CRAM, FASTA, VCF, BCF, and tabix files.

faq.question: Can PySAM replace samtools and bcftools?
faq.answer: PySAM exposes many samtools and bcftools operations, but complex pipelines may still use those tools directly.

faq.question: What coordinate system should I use?
faq.answer: Numeric PySAM calls usually use zero-based, half-open coordinates. VCF positions and region strings often use one-based coordinates.

faq.question: Is this skill suitable for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. It can support analysis workflows, but clinical interpretation requires validated pipelines and expert review.
